description_html:
The Maritime Inventory Routing Problem (MIRP) arises from global bulk shipping and involves both ship routing and inventory management. The problem not only determines routes from production (loading) ports to consumption (discharging) ports to minimize transportation costs, but also manages the inventory at these ports [Papageorgiou14]. [Papageorgiou14] introduced a mixed-integer programming core model of this problem class and developed a library of publicly available test instances (MIRPLib, mirplib.scl.gatech.edu).

Where the instances come from. The D-MIPLIB MIRP instances are the 118 instances (98 train + 20 test) of the “anonymous” benchmark of the ML4CO competition [Gasse22], a curated subset of MIRPLib whose variable/constraint names were anonymized. Every one of the 118 instances is numerically identical (same dimensions, nonzeros, coefficients, right-hand sides, bounds and objective coefficients) to exactly one MIRPLib MPS file. They come from three different MILP formulations, all of which are available on MIRPLib:

  • (A) MIRPLib Group 2 (33 instances; 4 in test): long-horizon, vessel-class arc-flow model of [Papageorgiou14] (instances LR1_DRxx_VCyy_Vzz_t{120,180,360}).
  • (B) Jiang–Grossmann discrete-time model (42 instances; 9 in test) [Jiang15] (MIRPLib files Maritime_Jiang_Grossmann_Group{1,2,3,5,6}_D-*).
  • (C) Jiang–Grossmann continuous-time model with port event points (43 instances; 7 in test) [Jiang15] (MIRPLib files Maritime_Jiang_Grossmann_Group{1,2,3,5,6}_E-*).

Hence the distribution is a mixture of formulations. Models (B) and (C) contain no general integer variables; model (A) contains binaries and general integers. The full formulations are given below; click a model to expand it.

(A) MIRPLib Group 2 model: vessel-class arc-flow formulation [Papageorgiou14]

Each port forms its own region; all instances have a single loading port. Vessels travel full from the loading port to a discharging port and empty back (only out-and-back trips), so loaded/discharged quantities are implied by the arcs used.

Sets and parameters.

  • \(\mathcal{T}=\{0,\dots,T-1\}\): time periods (days), \(T\in\{120,180,360\}\).
  • \(\mathcal{J}=\mathcal{J}^P\cup\mathcal{J}^C\): loading and discharging ports; \(\Delta_j=+1\) if \(j\in\mathcal{J}^P\), \(-1\) if \(j\in\mathcal{J}^C\).
  • \(\mathcal{VC}\): vessel classes; class \(vc\) has \(|\mathcal{V}_{vc}|\) identical vessels of capacity \(Q_{vc}\).
  • \(\mathcal{N}=\{(j,t): j\in\mathcal{J}, t\in\mathcal{T}\}\): regular nodes of the time-space network, plus a source node \(n_s\) and a sink node \(n_e\).
  • \(\mathcal{A}_{vc}\): arcs of class \(vc\): source arcs \((n_s,(j,t))\), waiting arcs \(((j,t),(j,t+1))\), inter-regional travel arcs \(((j,t),(j',t+\tau^{vc}_{jj'}))\) between a loading and a discharging port, and sink arcs \(((j,t),n_e)\). \(FS^{vc}_n\) / \(RS^{vc}_n\): arcs of class \(vc\) leaving / entering node \(n\). \(\mathcal{O}^{vc}_n\subseteq FS^{vc}_n\): the travel arcs and the sink arc leaving \(n\) (a vessel that takes one of them loads/discharges a full load \(Q_{vc}\) at \(n\)).
  • \(C^{vc}_a\): arc cost (source arc: port fee \(\pi_j\); waiting arc: 0; travel arc \((j,j')\): \(C^{vc}_{km}\delta_{jj'}\) (discounted by \(1-\gamma^{vc}\) when travelling empty) \(+\,\pi_{j'}\); sink arc from \((j,t)\): \(-(T-1-t)\rho\) with \(\rho=0.01\), a reward for each period remaining after \(t\)).
  • \(N^{vc}_n\): number of vessels of class \(vc\) that become available at node \(n\) (initial positions).
  • \(d_{j,t}\): production/consumption at port \(j\) in period \(t\); \(S^{\max}_j\): storage capacity (\(S^{\min}_j=0\)); \(s_{j,0}\): initial inventory; \(B_j\): berth limit.
  • \(P_t=P^{spot}(\gamma^{spot})^t\): unit penalty for lost production/stockout (spot market) in period \(t\) (decreasing in \(t\); \(P^{spot}=100\), \(\gamma^{spot}=0.999\) in the instances checked).

Variables. \(x^{vc}_a\): number of class-\(vc\) vessels using arc \(a\) (binary on travel arcs; integer in \(\{0,\dots,|\mathcal{V}_{vc}|\}\) on waiting and sink arcs; fixed on source arcs); \(s_{j,t}\ge 0\): inventory at port \(j\) at the start of period \(t\) (\(t=0,\dots,T\)); \(\alpha_{j,t}\ge 0\): lost production / unmet demand (spot-market slack).

\begin{align} \min\ & \sum_{vc\in\mathcal{VC}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}_{vc}} C^{vc}_a x^{vc}_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{J}}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} P_t\,\alpha_{j,t} \\ \text{s.t. } & \sum_{a\in FS^{vc}_n} x^{vc}_a-\sum_{a\in RS^{vc}_n} x^{vc}_a=0, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N},\ vc\in\mathcal{VC} \quad\text{(vessel flow balance)}\\ & x^{vc}_{(n_s,n)}=N^{vc}_n, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N},\ vc\in\mathcal{VC} \quad\text{(initial positions)}\\ & s_{j,t+1}=s_{j,t}+\Delta_j\Big(d_{j,t}-\sum_{vc\in\mathcal{VC}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal{O}^{vc}_{(j,t)}} Q_{vc}\,x^{vc}_a-\alpha_{j,t}\Big), && \forall j\in\mathcal{J},\ t\in\mathcal{T} \quad\text{(port inventory balance)}\\ & \sum_{vc\in\mathcal{VC}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal{O}^{vc}_{(j,t)}} x^{vc}_a\le B_j, && \forall j\in\mathcal{J},\ t\in\mathcal{T} \quad\text{(berth limit)}\\ & 0\le s_{j,t}\le S^{\max}_j,\ \ t=1,\dots,T; \quad s_{j,0}\ \text{fixed}; \quad \alpha_{j,t}\ge 0, && \forall j\in\mathcal{J}\\ & x^{vc}_a\in\{0,1\}\ \text{(travel arcs)},\quad x^{vc}_a\in\{0,\dots,|\mathcal{V}_{vc}|\}\ \text{(waiting and sink arcs)}. \end{align}

The model has \(|\mathcal{J}|\,T\,|\mathcal{VC}|\) flow-balance rows, \(|\mathcal{J}|\,T\) inventory rows and \(|\mathcal{J}|\,T\) berth rows (the source-arc fixings are variable bounds).

(B) Jiang–Grossmann discrete-time model [Jiang15]

In the Jiang–Grossmann instances, the sequence of ports visited by each ship is an input (parameter \(x_{v,n,m}=1\) if ship \(v\) sails directly from port \(n\) to port \(m\)); the model decides when ships wait, prepare, load/discharge and sail, so as to keep port inventories within bounds at minimum cost.

Sets and parameters.

  • \(\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{D}\cup\{o,e\}\): production ports \(\mathcal{P}\), consumption ports \(\mathcal{D}\), and a virtual origin \(o\) and virtual destination \(e\) of all ships; \(\mathcal{V}\): ships; \(\mathcal{T}=\{1,\dots,|\mathcal{T}|\}\): time periods (the horizon \(H\) divided into \(|\mathcal{T}|=2H\) periods).
  • \(x_{v,n,m}\in\{0,1\}\): given route of ship \(v\); \(\tau_{nm}\): sailing time in periods (\(\tau_{o,m}\ge 1\)).
  • \(B_n\): number of ships that can operate at port \(n\) simultaneously; \(R_p\) / \(R_d\): production / consumption per period; \(q_{v,p}\) / \(\delta_{v,d}\): amount loaded / discharged by ship \(v\) per period of operation; \(f_{v,n}\): number of preparation periods before operating; \(W_v\): maximum number of waiting periods per port; \(L_v\): ship capacity; \(S^{lo}_n,S^{up}_n\): port inventory bounds (0 for the virtual ports); \(S^0_n\): initial inventory.
  • Costs: \(c^{sf}_v\) fixed and \(c^{sv}_v\) load-dependent sailing cost per period sailed; \(c^{w}_{v,n}\) waiting cost; \(c^{o}_{v,n}\) cost per period of preparation or operation.

Variables. Binary: \(op_{v,n,t}\) (ship \(v\) operates at \(n\) in \(t\)), \(of_{v,n,t}\) (prepares for operation), \(wa_{v,n,t}\) (waits), \(sa_{v,n,m,t}\) (starts sailing from \(n\) to \(m\) in \(t\)). Continuous, nonnegative: \(st_{n,t}\) (port stock at the beginning of \(t\)), \(la_{v,t}\) (ship load at the beginning of \(t\)), \(\lambda^1_{v,n,m,t},\lambda^2_{v,n,m,t}\) (linearization of \(la_{v,t}\,sa_{v,n,m,t}\)). Let \(\bar{\mathcal{N}}=\mathcal{P}\cup\mathcal{D}\) and \(OP_{v,n,t}=op_{v,n,t}+of_{v,n,t}\).

\begin{align} \min\ & \sum_{v,n,m,t}\tau_{nm}\big(c^{sf}_v\,sa_{v,n,m,t}+c^{sv}_v\,\lambda^1_{v,n,m,t}\big)+\sum_{v,n,t}c^{w}_{v,n}\,wa_{v,n,t}+\sum_{v,n,t}c^{o}_{v,n}\big(of_{v,n,t}+op_{v,n,t}\big)\\ \text{s.t. } & sa_{v,n,m,t}\le x_{v,n,m}, && \forall v,n,m,t\\ & \sum_{m\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{e\}}\sum_{t} sa_{v,o,m,t}=1,\qquad \sum_{n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{o\}}\ \sum_{t\le|\mathcal{T}|-\tau_{ne}} sa_{v,n,e,t}=1, && \forall v\\ & \sum_{v}OP_{v,n,t}\le B_n, && \forall n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}},t\\ & \sum_{m\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{o\}} sa_{v,m,n,t-\tau_{mn}}+wa_{v,n,t-1}=of_{v,n,t}+wa_{v,n,t}, && \forall v,n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}},t\\ & OP_{v,n,t-1}=\sum_{m\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{e\}} sa_{v,n,m,t}+op_{v,n,t}, && \forall v,n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}},t\\ & OP_{v,n,t-1}\le OP_{v,n,t}+\sum_{m\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{e\}} sa_{v,n,m,t}, && \forall v,n,t\\ & op_{v,n,t-1}\ge \sum_{m\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}\cup\{e\}} sa_{v,n,m,t}, && \forall v,n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}},t\\ & \sum_{t'>t} of_{v,n,t'}+op_{v,n,t}\le 1, && \forall v,n,t\\ & st_{p,t+1}=st_{p,t}-\sum_v q_{v,p}\,op_{v,p,t}+R_p, && \forall p\in\mathcal{P},t<|\mathcal{T}|\\ & st_{d,t+1}=st_{d,t}+\sum_v \delta_{v,d}\,op_{v,d,t}-R_d, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},t<|\mathcal{T}|\\ & la_{v,t+1}=la_{v,t}+\sum_{p}q_{v,p}\,op_{v,p,t}-\sum_{d}\delta_{v,d}\,op_{v,d,t}, && \forall v,t<|\mathcal{T}|\\ & S^{lo}_p\le st_{p,|\mathcal{T}|}-\sum_v q_{v,p}\,op_{v,p,|\mathcal{T}|}+R_p\le S^{up}_p, && \forall p\in\mathcal{P}\\ & S^{lo}_d\le st_{d,|\mathcal{T}|}+\sum_v \delta_{v,d}\,op_{v,d,|\mathcal{T}|}-R_d\le S^{up}_d, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & S^{lo}_n\le st_{n,t}\le S^{up}_n, && \forall n,t\\ & la_{v,t}\le L_v\ \ \forall v,t,\qquad la_{v,|\mathcal{T}|}+\sum_{p}q_{v,p}\,op_{v,p,|\mathcal{T}|}-\sum_{d}\delta_{v,d}\,op_{v,d,|\mathcal{T}|}\le L_v, && \forall v\\ & \sum_t wa_{v,n,t}\le W_v, && \forall v,n\\ & \sum_t of_{v,n,t}=f_{v,n}\sum_m x_{v,m,n}, && \forall v,n\\ & \lambda^1_{v,n,m,t}+\lambda^2_{v,n,m,t}=la_{v,t},\quad \lambda^1_{v,n,m,t}\le L_v\,sa_{v,n,m,t},\quad \lambda^2_{v,n,m,t}\le L_v(1-sa_{v,n,m,t}), && \forall v,n,m,t\\ & st_{n,1}=S^0_n,\ \ la_{v,1}=0;\qquad op,of,wa,sa\in\{0,1\};\quad st,la,\lambda^1,\lambda^2\ge 0. \end{align}

(Terms with a time index outside \(\mathcal{T}\) are omitted. Variables and constraints are generated for all index combinations, so most \(sa\) variables are forced to 0 by the first constraint.)

(C) Jiang–Grossmann continuous-time model with port event points [Jiang15]

Same data as (B), but time is continuous on \([0,H]\) (distances \(\mathrm{dist}_{nm}\), preparation time \(t^f_{v,n}\) and handling time per unit \(t^v_{v,n}\) in time units; \(R_p,R_d\) are rates per time unit). Each port \(n\) has event points \(l\in\mathcal{L}_n=\{1,\dots,E_n\}\), with \(E_n=3\times\)(number of ship visits to \(n\)) (\(E_o=3|\mathcal{V}|\)). Let \(k_{v,n}=\sum_m x_{v,m,n}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that ship \(v\) visits \(n\).

Variables. Binary: \(y^s_{v,n,l}\), \(y^f_{v,n,l}\), \(y^e_{v,n,l}\) (ship \(v\) starts operation / finishes preparation / ends operation at event point \(l\) of port \(n\)). Continuous, nonnegative: event times \(T_{n,l}\); times \(t^a_{v,n}\) (arrival), \(t^o_{v,n}\) (start of operation), \(t^{fi}_{v,n}\) (end of preparation), \(t^l_{v,n}\) (departure), waiting time \(t^w_{v,n}\); amounts \(q_{v,p}\), \(r_{v,d}\) loaded/discharged; stock \(st_{n,l}\); ship load before/after operation \(la^1_{v,n},la^2_{v,n}\); linearization variables \(\phi^{f}_{v,n,l,l'}=y^f_{v,n,l}T_{n,l'}\), \(\phi^{e}_{v,n,l,l'}=y^e_{v,n,l}T_{n,l'}\), \(\psi^q_{v,p,l}=y^f_{v,p,l}q_{v,p}\), \(\psi^r_{v,d,l}=y^f_{v,d,l}r_{v,d}\) and their complements \(\bar\phi^{f},\bar\phi^{e},\bar\psi^q,\bar\psi^r\).

\begin{align} \min\ & \sum_v\Big[\sum_{n,m}x_{v,n,m}\,\mathrm{dist}_{nm}\big(c^{sf}_v+c^{sv}_v\,la^2_{v,n}\big)+\sum_n c^w_{v,n}\,t^w_{v,n}+\sum_{n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}}c^o_{v,n}\big(t^l_{v,n}-t^o_{v,n}\big)\Big]\\ \text{s.t. } & T_{n,l}\le H,\quad T_{n,l}\ge T_{n,l'}\ \ (l>l'), && \forall n,\ l,l'\in\mathcal{L}_n\\ & \sum_{l}y^s_{v,n,l}=\sum_{l}y^e_{v,n,l}=k_{v,n}\ (n\ne o),\quad \sum_{l}y^s_{v,o,l}=\sum_{l}y^e_{v,o,l}=1,\quad \sum_l y^f_{v,n,l}=\sum_l y^s_{v,n,l}, && \forall v,n\\ & |T_{n,l}-t^o_{v,n}|\le H(1-y^s_{v,n,l}),\ \ |T_{n,l}-t^{l}_{v,n}|\le H(1-y^e_{v,n,l}),\ \ |T_{n,l}-t^{fi}_{v,n}|\le H(1-y^f_{v,n,l}), && \forall v,n,l\in\mathcal{L}_n\\ & \sum_v\sum_{l'\le l}\big(y^s_{v,n,l'}-y^e_{v,n,l'}\big)\le B_n, && \forall n,l\in\mathcal{L}_n\\ & t^a_{v,n}=\sum_m x_{v,m,n}\big(t^l_{v,m}+\mathrm{dist}_{mn}\big)\ (n\ne o),\quad t^o_{v,n}\ge t^a_{v,n},\quad t^w_{v,n}=t^o_{v,n}-t^a_{v,n}, && \forall v,n\\ & t^{fi}_{v,n}=t^o_{v,n}+k_{v,n}t^f_{v,n},\quad t^l_{v,p}=t^{fi}_{v,p}+k_{v,p}t^v_{v,p}q_{v,p},\quad t^l_{v,d}=t^{fi}_{v,d}+k_{v,d}t^v_{v,d}r_{v,d}, && \forall v,n,p,d\\ & t^l_{v,o}=t^{fi}_{v,o},\quad t^l_{v,e}=t^o_{v,e}=t^a_{v,e}\le H,\quad t^w_{v,n}\le W_v\ (n\ne o), && \forall v,n\\ & st_{p,l+1}=st_{p,l}-\sum_v\sum_{l'\le l}\frac{\phi^f_{v,p,l',l+1}-\phi^e_{v,p,l',l+1}-\phi^f_{v,p,l',l}+\phi^e_{v,p,l',l}}{t^v_{v,p}}+R_p\big(T_{p,l+1}-T_{p,l}\big), && \forall p,\ l0\\ & S^{lo}_p\le st_{p,E_p}+R_p(H-T_{p,E_p})\le S^{up}_p,\quad S^{lo}_d\le st_{d,E_d}-R_d(H-T_{d,E_d})\le S^{up}_d, && \forall p,d \text{ with } E_n>0\\ & S^{lo}_n\le st_{n,l}\le S^{up}_n, && \forall n,l\in\mathcal{L}_n\\ & la^2_{v,p}=la^1_{v,p}+\sum_l\psi^q_{v,p,l},\quad la^2_{v,d}=la^1_{v,d}-\sum_l\psi^r_{v,d,l},\quad la^1_{v,n}=\sum_m x_{v,m,n}\,la^2_{v,m}\ (n\in\bar{\mathcal{N}}),\quad la^2_{v,p}\le L_v, && \forall v,p,d\\ & \phi^f_{v,n,l,l'}\le H y^f_{v,n,l},\ \ \bar\phi^f_{v,n,l,l'}\le H(1-y^f_{v,n,l}),\ \ \phi^f_{v,n,l,l'}+\bar\phi^f_{v,n,l,l'}=T_{n,l'}\ \ (\text{same for }\phi^e\text{ with }y^e), && \forall v,n,\ l,l'\in\mathcal{L}_n\\ & \psi^q_{v,p,l}\le L_v y^f_{v,p,l},\ \ \bar\psi^q_{v,p,l}\le L_v(1-y^f_{v,p,l}),\ \ \psi^q_{v,p,l}+\bar\psi^q_{v,p,l}=q_{v,p}\ \ (\text{same for }\psi^r\text{ with }r_{v,d}), && \forall v,p,d,l\\ & la^1_{v,o}=la^2_{v,o}=0;\qquad y^s,y^f,y^e\in\{0,1\};\quad \text{all other variables}\ \ge 0. \end{align}

In both Jiang–Grossmann models the objective is written in the instance files through a free variable equal to the total cost, which is minimized.

Medium: 118 instances (98 train / 20 test): 33 Group 2 [Papageorgiou14], 42 Jiang–Grossmann discrete-time, 43 Jiang–Grossmann continuous-time [Jiang15]
Group 2: 3–9 (1 loading + 2–8 discharging); J–G: 6 (2–4 loading + 2–4 discharging, plus 2 virtual)
Group 2: 6–40 vessels in 1–5 classes; J–G: 2–3 ships
Group 2: 120, 180 or 360 days; J–G: 60 or 70 time units (discrete-time model: 120 or 140 periods)

changes: Added the full formulation. The instances are NOT a single model: fingerprint matching shows the 118 ML4CO 'anonymous' instances (= HF train 98 + test 20) are a mixture of three MIRPLib formulations: MIRPLib Group 2 vessel-class arc-flow model (33), Jiang-Grossmann discrete-time model 'D' (42), Jiang-Grossmann continuous-time event-point model 'E' (43). All three formulations are written out.

Kept the existing intro prose (accurate); added a paragraph on provenance (ML4CO anonymous benchmark = curated MIRPLib subset, confirmed by ds4dm/ml4co-competition DATA.md: 'the third problem benchmark consists of a curated set of instances from the MIRPLIB library').

New reference needed: [Jiang15] Y. Jiang and I. E. Grossmann, 'Alternative mixed-integer linear programming models of a maritime inventory routing problem', Computers & Chemical Engineering 77:147-161, 2015, doi:10.1016/j.compchemeng.2015.03.005. (The Group 2 model itself is documented in D. J. Papageorgiou, 'A mixed-integer linear programming formulation for Group 2 maritime inventory routing instances', MIRPLib technical note Group2_MIP_Model.pdf, 2013; it can be cited as part of [Papageorgiou14].)
Proposed domain-parameter columns: instance sources, # ports, # vessels, planning horizon (single 'Medium' row, values given as ranges per sub-family because the distribution is a mixture).

Table statistics (columns kept as-is, but note): the current '# Var B = 0' is wrong. Recomputing over all 118 instances reproduces '# Var I' = 15080.57, '# Var C' = 19576.15 and '# Constr' = 44429.7 exactly, but '# Var I' counts binaries and general integers together; the split is # Var B = 13532.91 and general (non-binary) integer = 1547.66. Suggest changing to # Var B 13532.91 / # Var I 1547.66.
verification: Downloaded the full HF MIRP/medium test.csv (20 instances) and train.csv (98 instances) and all MIRPLib MPS files (Group 1: 28, Group 2: 72, Jiang-Grossmann: 200). For every instance computed a fingerprint (dimensions, nnz, sorted multisets of matrix coefficients, row bounds, column bounds, objective coefficients). All 118 instances match exactly one MIRPLib file each: 33 Group 2 (LR1_DR02..DR08, VC01..VC05, V6..V40, t120/t180/t360), 42 Jiang-Grossmann *_D-* (groups 1,2,3,5,6), 43 Jiang-Grossmann *_E-* (groups 1,2,3,5,6). No Group 1 (Papageorgiou core-model) instances and no J-G 'S'/'RS' or group-4 instances. Test split: 4 G2, 9 D, 7 E. Mapping saved in research/mirp_mapping.json.

Group 2 model checked against the named MIRPLib MPS files (LR1_DR02_VC01_V6a_t360 = test t7, LR1_DR08_VC05_V40a_t120 = test t1): row families flowBalance (|J|*T*|VC|, '=', 0 RHS), invBalanceRegion (|J|*T, '=', coefficients +-Q_vc on travel and sink arcs, +-1 on alpha, RHS = +-d), berthLimit (|J|*T, '<=', RHS B_j in {1,3}); row counts match for t7 (3240), t1 (7560), t3 (4200), t14 (5400). Travel arcs binary with cost 213-2193 (incl. port fee); waiting arcs integer [0,|V_vc|] cost 0; sink arcs integer [0,|V_vc|] cost -(T-t)rho in [-3.59,0]; source arcs fixed by bounds to initial vessel positions, cost = port fee (21-85); alpha cost 100*0.999^t; s_{j,0} fixed to initial inventory; two dummy variables fixed at 0.

J-G discrete-time model: reproduced the exact constraint count of Maritime_D.gms (with 'Onsail' excluded as in the GAMS model statement) for group 1 (8 nodes, 2 ships, 120 periods): 73483 rows; variable counts 21120 binaries (op,of,wa: 3*2*8*120, sa: 2*8*8*120) and 31921 continuous (st 960 + la 240 + 2*15360 + objective var) match; groups 2/3/5/6 (8 nodes, 3 ships, 140 periods): 36960 B / 55301 C / 126621 rows match.

J-G continuous-time model: with E_n = 3 x (number of ship visits) from the route table x, binary count 3*|V|*sum_n E_n matches (group 1: 162; group 2: 405), and the row count of Maritime_E.gms (StEtEn and Ysetrans excluded per the model statement, empty rows for unvisited ports dropped) gives 2599 for group 1, matching the instance.
In all J-G instances the objective is a single free variable with objective coefficient 1 defined by the cost equation (GAMS export), sense min. Group 2 instances minimize directly.
open_questions: Confidence: very high for the identification of each instance (exact numeric fingerprint match to a unique MIRPLib file). Formulation (A) is verified family-by-family against named MPS rows; (B) and (C) are transcribed from the MIRPLib GAMS files Maritime_D.gms / Maritime_E.gms and verified via exact row/variable counts, not row-by-row coefficients.

The Jiang-Grossmann paper [Jiang15] could not be accessed (paywall); the description of (B)/(C) follows the GAMS code on MIRPLib. In those files the ship routes x(v,n,m) are input parameters, so the J-G instances are fixed-route scheduling/inventory problems; the paper may describe a more general model. Time units of the J-G data (TimePeriod = 60 or 70) are not stated in the files (likely days).

Whether HF test.csv corresponds to the ML4CO public 'valid' split or the post-competition 'test' split was not checked (would require the ML4CO Google-Drive archives). The ML4CO paper reports three clusters (Anonymous-c1/c2/c3), consistent with the three formulations found here.
The domain-parameter values are ranges over a mixture; the site may prefer to split the row by sub-family (G2 / J-G D / J-G E) if per-row values are desired.
